title: A Debt for the Border
premise: Yara Yarrow, a private security contractor who survives by being unattributable, receives a meeting request from a handler she buried six months ago. Following it into a border-town safehouse, she learns the dead man faked his death to expose a trafficking pipeline run by the agency that once employed them both, and he needs her to extract his star witness: a defector who may be bait dangled to flush out every ghost like Yara. When the extraction turns into an ambush and her handler is killed for real, Yara must choose between vanishing again or burning her carefully built invisibility to get the defector across the border alive. She delivers him to a journalist at devastating personal cost—her cover, her assets, her freedom—and ends the book in custody, finally on the record.
about_author: Elodie Fairweather is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent a decade moving people and cargo through checkpoints she still won't name. She writes thrillers about the invisible workers of the security world from a farmhouse whose location she changes often.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Working a forgettable protection job in a border town, Yara receives an encrypted meeting invite signed by Marcus Hale—the handler she watched buried months ago. Against every instinct, she verifies the cryptogram only he would know and goes. The emotional beat: dread sharpening into reluctant hope that the one person who understood her trade isn't gone.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. In a decaying safehouse, Hale reveals a trafficking pipeline protected by their old agency and asks Yara to extract Nadia Reyes, a defector holding its ledger. Yara suspects Nadia is bait meant to draw out contractors like herself, but agrees when she recognizes the girl's terror as genuine. The emotional beat: suspicion warring with the pull of found family.

chapters.title: Crossing Fire
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Yara and Nadia. The extraction convoy is ambushed at a river checkpoint—Hale is killed for real this time, confirming someone inside sold them out. Yara and Nadia flee on foot through the desert while Nadia confesses she suspected she was bait all along. The emotional beat: grief transmuting into fury, two strangers becoming allies.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Cornered with no route out, Yara realizes invisibility was always the trap keeping her complicit through silence. She contacts investigative journalist Priya Anand, trades the ledger and her testimony for Nadia's safe passage, and surrenders to federal agents as the story breaks. The emotional beat: costly resolution—justice achieved outside the law's protection, paid for with everything Yara built to disappear.
